title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache & parallelism
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows have grown slow and brittle. Lint/test/release are tightly coupled, causing long queue times and frequent cache pollution. This PR splits the workflows into dedicated lint, unit/integration test, and release pipelines, unblocks parallelism across repositories, and centralizes cache key hygiene utilities. Goals: reduce CI wall-clock time, improve cache hit rates, make release automation more transparent, and simplify debug surface.

What I changed (summary):
- Split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows: lint.yml, test.yml, release.yml. Each workflow has a focused matrix and clear resource limits.
- Introduced tools/ci/cache-utils.sh and scripts/ci/setup-parallelism.sh to standardize cache keys and runner parallelism settings across repos.
- Added Makefile.ci targets to provide reproducible steps for local dev (make ci-lint, ci-test).
- Minor docs: docs/ci/README.md with runbooks and troubleshooting.
- Release workflow now requires explicit approvals for production releases and emits a changelog artifact (used by release automation).

Checklist (completed):
- [x] Split workflows and validate each in feature branch.
- [x] Add cache key normalization + version bump for action versions.
- [x] Run test workflow across redwood, redwood-sdk-python, and redwood-docs to validate parallelism.
- [x] Update docs with troubleshooting and migration notes.
- [x] Notify platforms and oncall about rollout schedule.

Rollout plan: merge to main, enable workflows in staged mode for 24h (monitor queue and cache hit metrics), then full rollout. We will revert with the provided rollback tag if we observe regressions.

Notes on backward compatibility: This change is CI-only and does not affect runtime code. Actions versions were bumped where necessary; pinned major versions remain unchanged. Repos that consume reusable workflows will continue to work but should migrate to the new cache-utils.sh entries within 2 weeks to avoid degraded cache performance.

Related: ENG-1142 (CI parallelism), ENG-1199 (release automation hygiene), SUP-879 (support escalations on flaky CI).

release_notes: Split CI workflows: lint, test, release. Added cache hygiene utilities and local CI targets. Improves CI parallelism and cache hit rates; no runtime changes.
additional_notes: Monorepo consumers should migrate to tools/ci/cache-utils.sh within 2 weeks to benefit from normalized cache keys and avoid transient cache misses. Monitoring: ci.queue_time and ci.cache_hit_rate dashboards updated in observability-pack.
